messages.author: 1f723d378f24adbb
messages.subject: bad mixing and misestimation for Dirichlet hyperprior
parts:
Hi,

I am working on a problem where I noticed that estimating using
simulated data does not deliver a good posterior. I have simplified to a
simple self-contained example below, in the hope that someone can point
out the error I made. The problem is complex because of censoring.

I have N individuals, for each of them I have

1. a data point m,

2. a parameter pair (alpha,beta) which are the first two values from a
simplex (I parametrize this as Dirichlet, not essential to what I am
doing but seemed natural),

3. a parameter w, drawn from a known distribution (for simplicity here),

4. a binomially distributed observation, with probability beta/(1-alpha).

The sample only contains variables for which m/w < (1-alpha)/alpha.

(alpha,beta,w) are interesting to me for each individual, the rest are
nuisance parameters.

To capture the constraint, I obtain w with a transformation from a [0,1]
interval, correcting for the Jacobian. I attach the code for generating
the data and checking the posterior (in R, with plots etc), and the Stan
model.

My problems are

1. that the alpha's are mis-estimated, they all seem to be around the
same value for everyone,

2. the a parameters of the hyperprior for (alpha,beta,_) have bad
mixing, especially the first Dirichlet parameter.

Maybe these are related. Any hints on what I am doing wrong would be
appreciated. I don't think this is a Stan bug, rather user error, but I
can't find the source of it.

Best,

Tamas

messages.author: 1f723d378f24adbb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] bad mixing and misestimation for Dirichlet hyperprior
parts:
Hi Rob,

In the data generating process, the observation is kept only iff

w[i]/m[i] < (1-alpha[i])/alpha[i]

(see the R code where I simulate data).

This is a nonlinear constraint on the (w,alpha) space. The easiest way
to express this (for me) was to draw an alpha and a v, and then
transform w from the v.

The Jacobian is triangular, so I think (hope?) that I am doing it
correctly, but if you notice any errors, please tell me.

Thanks for looking at this.

Best,

Tamas

parts:
> On Dec 3, 2014, at 6:50 PM, Tamas Papp <tkp...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Rob,
>
> In the data generating process, the observation is kept only iff
>
> w[i]/m[i] < (1-alpha[i])/alpha[i]
>
> (see the R code where I simulate data).

Were the other observations and censored and if so, do you know
how many censorings were done for the data set?

Otherwise, if you just simulate from a model and throw
some of the observations away, you shouldn't expect to
recover the parameters because the model doesn't match the
data generation process.

For example, consider generating data according to normal(0,1)
and then throwing away any negative observations. You're not
going to expect a sample mean of 0 or sample sd of 1.

To do this right, you need to record how many observations were
below 0 and use the normal cdf to model them.

There's a chapter in the manual on data censoring.

- Bob
